title: Cobalt runtime scratchpad - Aurora
content:
Quick log / brain dump, not for prime time.

Context + goal:
- Running day shift solo. Primary focus: reduce intermittent p99 spikes and get a minimal, repeatable repro for the KV cache regression observed after quantized-kv rollout.
- Keep a small set of safe rollbacks and mitigations I can apply quickly if canary goes bad.

Observations so far (what I saw today):
- 11:20 UTC: p99 on model-mq-13 jumped from 120ms -> 490ms for ~5m window. CPU/GPU usage flat, no obvious throttle.
- 11:21 UTC: quick look at route logs shows a backlog on worker-3 (hostable-03). Recent kernel build (rfe/kv-compact-optim) deployed yesterday evening to staging then to canary (10%).
- tail of logs: repeated "kv-cache-miss -> reload -> out-of-memory-ish eviction" entries then a flurry of small GC pauses (~3–6ms) on hostable-03.
- NVLink stats: slightly higher average transfer latency but within noise. Nothing obvious on NUMA counters.

Immediate hypotheses (order from most likely to least):
1) new compacted-KV allocator has a race under certain prefix collision patterns -> temporary double-alloc and eviction loop.
2) batching math change (attempt to rehydrate small prefixes into a single cache entry) causing bigger-than-expected entries -> memory churn + eviction thrash.
3) scheduler is pinning too many hot model shards to hostable-03 during canary -> microburst queueing.
4) unrelated infra blip (network hiccup) that only amplified because of reduced cache headroom in canary variants.

Quick triage steps I ran (for reproducibility):
- grep logs for "kv-cache-miss" + hostable-03 between 11:15–11:30 -> got 186 lines. Saved to /tmp/aurora/kv-miss-20260311.log
- pulled memory maps from hostable-03 (admin tool) -> snapshot: free mem 8.6GB, cached 11GB, swap unused. No process OOM kills.
- heap hist: invocation sizes showed steady median tokens=24 but a heavy tail of >512 for 0.7% of requests (these were mainly reranker flows).

Things to try (quick, low-risk):
- Roll canary down to 0% (safe, do via console) if spike repeats and we see same pattern. Keep canary artifacts tagged.
- Temporarily disable compacted-KV allocator via feature flag (flag=kv_compact=false) on canary subset and observe.
- Add short-term alert on "kv-eviction-rate > 50/min" for a route-level alarm to Paging.

Longer-term debug plan (needs pair or PR):
- Add deterministic reproducer: craft a workload mix that hits the >512 token path repeatedly while interleaving small prefixes that trigger compacting. Script: mix generator + local kv-runner harness.
- Add extra logging in allocator: lightweight counters for attempted-alloc-size, post-compact-size, eviction-triggered count. Ensure logs are rate-limited.
- Investigate pointer-stability guarantees in compacted allocator: look for missing barrier in concurrent shrink path.
- Perf isolate: run microbench comparing old allocator vs compacted with live workload using --latency-sampler.

Notes / commands I used:
- ./tools/logs.sh hostable-03 "kv-cache-miss" 2026-03-11T11:15 2026-03-11T11:30 > /tmp/aurora/kv-miss-20260311.log
- ssh admin@hostable-03 sudo heapdump --summary > /tmp/aurora/heap-summary-11-20.txt
- python infra/kv-replay/generate.py --mix reranker:0.01,chat:0.89,embeddings:0.1 --seq-tail-heavy --rate 100/s --duration 600s

To-do (prioritized):
1) (ASAP) Create a high-signal bug issue with minimal repro steps + attach log excerpt (me). Include "probable regressor: compacted-kv allocator". TAG: eng-serving-runtime, label: severity-P2.
2) (Today) Toggle kv_compact feature flag off on canary -> monitor for 30m. (If returns to baseline, escalate to rollback plan.)
3) (Today) Add temporary alert channel for eviction-rate > 50/min. (SRE assist Linus?)
4) (Tomorrow) Pair with Samir on allocator codepath review — focus on shrink/merge code.
5) (This sprint) Implement lightweight counters and a flag to force non-compacted mode per model shard for debugging.

Stretch items / nice-to-haves:
- Heatmap dashboard of per-shard average entry size + eviction frequency over last 7d. Would show if compacted entries are abnormally big.
- Integration test that floods small prefix patterns to ensure allocator doesn't grow unbounded.

Meeting notes from quick sync with Lina (11:45):
- Lina: "If this is allocator-race, we'll see spikes only under certain traffic mixes. Start with toggling compacted flag and check. Also, try the repro harness that reproduces >512 token tail."
- Action: Lina will open SRE runbook entry to include post-mortem steps and exact checklist for runbook toggles.

Risk/rollback matrix (for on-call):
- If p99 stays >300ms for >10m across >25% traffic -> rollback canary to previous build and open incident.
- If toggle of kv_compact=false reduces eviction rate by >70% -> promote temporary rollback and schedule hotfix.
- If toggle doesn't help -> consider capacity redistribution (move some shards off hostable-03) as short-term mitigation.

Random micro-thoughts to capture (brain-storm):
- Could compacted-KV produce pathological growth on certain prefix sets (e.g., many small prefixes that merge into one large entry)? Need to quantify merge factor distribution.
- Forcing a soft cap per-entry after compact might make recompaction more predictable at cost of space. Worth testing.
- We should consider passive sampling of heavy-tail sequences and pre-populating a shared cold-cache to reduce cold thrash.

Next immediate steps I will take before EOD:
- Create bug issue with logs + initial triage notes.
- Toggle kv_compact on canary and watch for 30m. Post quick note to #runtime-kernel with status.
- If toggle shows improvement, prepare rollback PR template and notify PM/Release.

Notes-to-self: keep documentation of any temporary toggles (feature flags) in the incident doc; don't leave them on longer than 24–48h without explicit owner.

End of dump.

-- Ava
(quick meta: meant to be a compact, action-oriented log so I can handoff to next shift)
